around.headline: Travel bus crew assault driver in Bengaluru road-rage case
around.summary: The Times of India reports a travel bus crew assaulted a driver in a road-rage case in the city. If a traffic spat starts, stay in your vehicle, note the registration number and call 112 rather than arguing.

around.headline: Gym trainer killed at party in Bengaluru; four held
around.summary: The Hindu and Deccan Herald report a trainer died after a fight at a gym anniversary party and four were held; NDTV places the argument inside a client's apartment, so details differ between outlets. If a party argument turns physical, leave and call 112 rather than stepping in.

around.headline: Rain waterlogs key roads; Chandapura jam traps weekend returnees for hours
around.summary: The Times of India reports waterlogging on key roads after heavy rain, and The Hindu reports an hours-long jam at Chandapura as the weekend return rush peaked. With rain forecast again today, allow extra time and skip flooded underpasses.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Traffic restrictions begin on Race Course Road
around.summary: Urbanacres reports traffic restrictions have begun on Race Course Road. Plan an alternate route, especially in wet-weather peak hours.

around.headline: 10-year plan: nine townships, 312 km Metro and 210 km ring road for Bengaluru region
around.summary: The Times of India and Deccan Herald report CM Shivakumar's long-term plan to ease pressure on the city with nine townships, 312 km of Metro and a 210 km ring road. These are plans, not timelines, so don't expect relief on your commute soon.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: IndiGo raises fuel charge by up to 50% ahead of festive travel
around.summary: The Times of India reports IndiGo has raised its fuel charge by up to 50%. Check the final fare including charges before paying, and book early if you're flying during the festive season.

around.headline: India-US trade deal talks have plateaued, says Finance Ministry
around.summary: The Hindu reports the Finance Ministry says further demands and concessions in the talks will be very difficult. A deal that affects export-linked jobs in Bengaluru's tech and manufacturing sectors is not imminent.

street_smart.title: Your phone buzzes with an SMS: 'Pending traffic challan on your vehicle. Pay within 24 hours to avoid a higher fine or licence suspension', with a link to pay. You do ride a two-wheeler and aren't sure whether you have any fines. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Deccan Herald, Oct 5: Bengaluru has traffic fines worth Rs 3,000 crore unpaid. With so many pending fines in the news, fake 'challan' payment links are a common pretext for phishing; this mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The message has an urgent tone and a short link. It doesn't mention any location, offence or date.

choices.text: Tap the link and pay quickly. It is only a few hundred rupees.
choices.feedback: The link opens a copy of a payment page that captures your card or UPI details and OTP, so the loss can be far bigger than the 'fine'. Urgency and a deadline are used to stop you thinking.

choices.text: Don't tap the link. Check your vehicle number on the official Karnataka traffic police / Parivahan e-challan site, typed in yourself, and pay only there if a challan exists.
choices.feedback: A real challan has a vehicle number, date, place and offence you can look up on the official site. Typing the address yourself bypasses fake links.

choices.text: Reply 'STOP' or call the number in the SMS to ask what it's about.
choices.feedback: Replying confirms your number is active and a caller can then pressure you for details. Ignore it and verify independently.

choices.text: Forward the SMS and link to friends to warn them, and tap it once to see what it is.
choices.feedback: Opening an unknown link can install malware or prompt for credentials, and forwarding spreads it. Report it instead.

takeaways: Verify a challan only on the official site you type yourself; never through an SMS link.
Report scam messages at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 immediately if money was paid.
Urgent deadlines, threats of suspension and short links are red flags for phishing.

quiz.question: How many km of Metro does the 10-year plan for the Bengaluru region propose?
quiz.why: The plan also has nine townships and a 210 km ring road. Namma Metro is the city's rapid transit system.

quiz.question: By up to how much has IndiGo raised its fuel charge?
quiz.why: The Times of India reports the increase of up to 50% ahead of festive travel. A fuel charge is a separate line on top of the base fare.

quiz.question: Who does Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro face in the presidential runoff?
quiz.why: The Hindu reports Bolsonaro beat polls in the first round. Brazil uses a two-round system when no candidate wins a majority.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution vests the superintendence of elections in the Election Commission?
quiz.why: Article 324 covers elections to Parliament, state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
quiz.why: Oxygen is about 21%. Nitrogen is mostly inert in air and plants need it fixed by bacteria or fertilisers.
